narrationTexts: Found it — the noise is all deprecation warnings, but the actual failure is a real bug in the link stage. `resolveRetries` in `src/core/options.js:7` still reads `options.retries`, but the bumped bundler now passes `{ retryCount }`, so `.toFixed` throws on `undefined`. First bug is resolved; now the second, real bug surfaces: `isBackoffEnabled` in `src/net/retryPolicy.js` throws when the flag is `undefined`, but the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` (not `false`) — that's a legitimate default case, not an error.
finalText:
Build's clean now (exit 0). Two real bugs were hiding behind the deprecation-warning noise, both caused by the bundler bump changing its options/config shape:

1. **`src/core/options.js`** — `resolveRetries` still read `options.retries`, but the bumped bundler now passes `{ retryCount }`, so it crashed on `undefined.toFixed()`. Fixed to read `options.retryCount`.
2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js`** — `isBackoffEnabled` only accepted explicit `true`/`false` and threw on anything else, but the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` instead of `false`. Added an `undefined` → `false` (disabled) case.

The remaining 8 warnings are just deprecation noise (`fs.exists`, `Buffer()`, punycode, etc.) from the version bump — not blocking, but worth cleaning up separately if you want to get ahead of future Node/dependency removals.
